explanation: A carrot is a vegetable — the others are all fruit.
A table is furniture — the others are all animals.
A dog is an animal — the others are all colours.
July is a month — the others are all days of the week.
'Blue' is a colour — the others are all numbers.
A teacher is a job — the others are all family members.
'Happy' is an adjective — the others are all action verbs.
'Dog' is a noun — the others are all subject pronouns.
'Table' is a noun — the others are all adjectives.
Bread is food — the others are all drinks.
A shoe is clothing — the others are all parts of the body.
'Kitchen' is a room — the others all describe the weather.
'Run' is an action verb — the others are forms of 'be'.
A banana is a fruit — the others are all kinds of transport.
A chair is an object — the others are all feelings.
'Goed' is not a word — the others are correct irregular past tenses.
'Good' is a base adjective — the others are comparatives.
'Blue' is a colour — the others are adverbs of frequency.
'Ran' is an irregular past tense — the others are regular '-ed' verbs.
A hospital is a place — the others are all jobs.
Monday is a day — the others are all seasons.
'Careful' is an adjective — the others are all adverbs.
'She' is a subject pronoun — the others are possessive adjectives.
A guitar is a musical instrument — the others are all sports.
A sandwich is food — the others are all drinks.
'Is' is present tense — the others are all past tense.
'Biggest' is a superlative — the others are comparatives.
A garden is outside the house — the others are all rooms inside.
An apple is a fruit — the others are all dairy products.
'Swimming' is an '-ing' form — the others are past simple verbs.
'Ago' is used with the past simple — since, for and yet go with the present perfect.
'Careful' is an adjective — the others are nouns ending in '-ness'.
'Athlete' is a person — the others are sports activities.
'Want' is an ordinary verb — the others are modal verbs.
'Beauty' is a noun — the others are all adjectives.
'Beautiful' is an adjective — the others are all phrasal verbs.
'Tired' is a normal adjective — the others are strong (extreme) adjectives.
'Teach' is a verb — the others are people/jobs ending in '-er' or '-or'.
'Disappear' is a verb — the others are adjectives with a negative prefix.
'Apples' is countable — the others are uncountable nouns.
An author is a person — the others are things you read.
'Did see' is past simple — the others are present perfect.
'Interested' describes a feeling ('-ed'); the others describe the cause ('-ing').
'Homework' goes with 'do' — the others all collocate with 'make'.
'So' shows a result — the others all show contrast.
'Moreover' adds information — the others signal contrast or concession.
'Ugly' is negative — the others are positive words for beautiful scenery.
'Reluctant' means unwilling — the others all mean willing/enthusiastic.
'Annoyed' is mild irritation — the others all mean extremely surprised.
'In addition' adds a point — the others all introduce a contrast.
'Will have' refers to the future — the others speculate about the past.
'Generous' is about giving — the others all describe being strong-willed.
'Childish' is an adjective — the others are nouns ending in '-hood'.
'Table and chair' is literal — the others are all idioms.
'Frequently' means often — the others all mean 'almost not'.
'Shout' is about volume — the others are about indirect meaning.
'Economy' is a noun — the others are all adjectives.
'Therefore' shows a result — the others signal contrast or concession.
'Worsen' means to make worse — the others all mean to reduce or relieve.
'What's up' is very informal — the others are formal/polite expressions.
'Careless' means not careful — the others all mean extremely careful.
'Consequently' shows result — the others all signal concession/contrast.
'Scarce' means rare — the others all mean found everywhere.
'Declare' is direct and open — the others all mean to suggest indirectly.
'Garbled' means unclear — the others all mean clear and easy to follow.
'Stem from' shows cause (effect to cause) — the others mean to cause or produce.
'Evasive' means avoiding the truth — the others all mean honest and direct.
'Alleviate' means to ease — the others all mean to make worse.
'Definitive' means final and certain — the others all mean not yet fixed.
'Trivial' means unimportant — the others all mean extremely important.
'Indisputably' presents something as fact — the others hedge a personal opinion.
'Dwindle' means to shrink — the others all mean to grow rapidly.
'Cohesive' is an adjective — the others are all nouns.
'Idealistic' is about ideals — the others all mean down-to-earth and practical.
'Because of' gives a reason — the others all mean 'although / even with'.
